turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Of course! I will think out loud with one example.
I cook dinner. My dad cooks dinner.
First I ask: who? "My dad" means "he". Then I add -s: cook becomes cooks.
Rule: with he, she or it, the verb takes -s.
Right: She cooks every evening. Wrong: She cook every evening.
Now you try. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
